topic: What trade-offs exist between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas?
response: For SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas, increasing the array size beyond 16x16 leads to a trade-off between good performance and compact configuration. Larger array sizes result in higher insertion loss due to increased SIW length, decreasing radiation efficiency from 70% to 27.5%. This is attributed to the high insertion loss of the substrate, estimated at 0.034 dB/mm at 60 GHz.
reference_context: The reference context discusses the design and performance of a wideband high-gain hybrid integrated plate array antenna for V-band inter-satellite links. It compares the radiation efficiency of SIW arrays with different aperture sizes, highlighting the trade-offs between array size and efficiency.
